title: Honest Interval Length for a Homogeneous Log-Odds Effect with a Rough Prognostic Logit
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; math PASS with no findings, score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4. Main independent validity gate confirms downgrade.
gap_reasons: The contribution remains confined to one covariate dimension, one fixed smoothness exponent, known uniform design and fair assignment, limiting its significance as a general inference framework.

The conservative calibration and large constants leave practical interval performance unestablished, so the projected paper score reflects a scoped theoretical characterization rather than a demonstrated broadly usable procedure.
proof_attempt_summary: One scoped D-1 revision removed a duplicate wrapper; one D0 solve then established the informal sharp frontier n^(-1/2)+r n^(-2/7), one radius-blind ambiently 90%-honest interval, and a matching homogeneous-effect converse on the unchanged model. Independent PR and maximality audits and the D0.5 math panel passed, but cold novelty review graded the narrow delivered package subfield below field (7.2 < 7.4), with no bounded in-scope improvement. No formalization or Lean verification was attempted; the remaining theorem-level positioning finding is editorial, and no seed was mathematically refuted.
tldr: For the prescribed randomized binary-outcome class with a homogeneous conditional log-odds effect and a Hölder-1/10 prognostic logit, the sharp ambient-honest expected interval length is \(J_n(r)\asymp n^{-1/2}+r n^{-2/7}\), with transition \(r\asymp n^{-3/14}\). One explicit radius-independent total interval is finite-sample \(90\%\)-honest over the full class and attains this order simultaneously for every evaluation radius; a matching original-record converse retains one scalar homogeneous effect in every alternative.
gap: Existing homogeneous-logistic and binary-DINA inference establishes first-order coefficient guarantees under nuisance conditions, while pairwise inference separates stochastic error from localization bias. The checked theorems do not characterize \(J_n(r)\) for the complete specified \(\beta=1/10\) class under ambient finite-sample honesty.
fill: The kernel joins confidence-region inversion with an original-record homogeneous-effect testing comparison. It determines the rate, its transitions, one simultaneous interval and a matching all-procedure lower bound in one unchanged experiment.
